S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S056.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
S056.description: Excessive anxiety and worry (expectant apprehension) occurring persistently about a number of events or activities.

subtypes.Chronic Worry: Worry occurs more days than not for at least 6 months.
subtypes.Generalized Worry: Worry is not confined to specific topics but spreads to various domains like work, school, family, and finances.
subtypes.Catastrophizing: Jumping to conclusions that minor mistakes or events will lead to irreversible disasters.
subtypes.Intolerance of Uncertainty: Unable to tolerate future uncertainty, trapped in 'what if' questions.

S057.name: Uncontrollable_Worry
S057.description: The subjective experience of finding it difficult to stop or control the worry.

subtypes.Failure to Control: Unable to regulate worry despite efforts to stop or distract oneself.
subtypes.Intrusive Worry: Worries suddenly intrude into the mind and interfere with focus while doing other tasks.
subtypes.Chaining of Worry: One worry triggers another in a chain reaction, escalating to catastrophic thoughts.

S058.name: Restlessness_Tension
S058.description: Restlessness, or feeling keyed up or on edge.

subtypes.Feeling Keyed Up: Feeling anxious and wound up like a spring, unable to stay still.
subtypes.Physical Tension: The entire body feels stiff and tense, unable to relax.
subtypes.Nervousness: Nerves are on edge, being startled easily by minor sounds or stimuli.

S059.name: Concentration_Difficulty
S059.description: Difficulty concentrating or mind going blank.

subtypes.Interference by Worry: Unable to focus on the task at hand because worries keep surfacing.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Attention is scattered due to anxiety, making it hard to focus on one thing for long.
subtypes.Mind Going Blank: Suddenly the mind goes empty or white, and no thoughts occur.

info.persona: Anabella Garcia is a hyper‑organized tech enthusiast who balances intense anxiety with a vibrant love for art, dance, and community mentorship, often juggling meticulous work projects with spontaneous creative bursts while they constantly seek harmony between structure and spontaneity.
info.professional_persona: Anabella Garcia combines disciplined organization and bilingual technical expertise to excel as a computer support specialist, mastering Windows, macOS, Linux, Active Directory, and scripting while they mentor peers and aspiring women in tech.
info.cultural_background: Anabella is a first‑generation Mexican‑American raised in a bilingual household that celebrated both Mexican traditions and Texan culture. She speaks Spanish fluently and English natively, and she actively participates in community events such as Día de los Muertos altar installations, Mexican Independence Day festivals, and local Cinco de Mayo celebrations in Plano. Her family places importance on close‑knit relationships, shared meals, and respect for cultural heritage, which she honors through cooking, music, and storytelling. At the same time, she embraces the entrepreneurial spirit and diversity of the Dallas‑Fort Worth area, blending her Mexican roots with contemporary American lifestyle.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Anabella’s free time reflects her eclectic personality; she regularly visits local art galleries and museums, and she enjoys painting watercolors inspired by Mexican folk motifs. She loves salsa and bachata dancing, often attending community dance nights. Cooking traditional Mexican dishes like mole and tamales is a creative outlet that connects her to her heritage. Outdoor activities such as hiking the Dallas‑Fort Worth trail system with friends satisfy her energetic, sociable side. She participates in tech meetups and hackathons, where she can explore new ideas. To manage her anxiety, Anabella practices yoga, meditation, and journaling, and she sometimes joins mindfulness workshops.
info.sports_persona: Anabella Garcia stays active by hiking the Dallas‑Fort Worth trail network with the DFW Trail Trekkers club, dancing salsa and bachata at the local Sabor Latino studio, and cheering on the Dallas Mavericks while they participate in a weekly recreational soccer league.
info.arts_persona: Anabella Garcia channels their love for visual storytelling into watercolor paintings inspired by folk motifs, drawing influence from Frida Kahlo, Diego Rivera, and contemporary muralist Jorge González, while they frequent exhibitions at the Dallas Museum of Art and enjoy salsa classics by Celia Cruz and Marc Anthony.
info.travel_persona: Anabella Garcia prefers curated getaways that blend cultural immersion and tech curiosity, having explored Mexico City’s historic neighborhoods, visited Oaxaca for its culinary scene, trekked the Camino Real in Spain, and planned a future road trip to Austin’s music festivals and the Hill Country’s vineyards while they balance travel planning with a demanding work schedule.
info.culinary_persona: Anabella Garcia delights in preparing traditional mole with dark chocolate, pasilla, and sesame seeds, rolling handmade tamales with masa and pork, and experimenting with fresh corn tortillas, while they also enjoy the occasional taco al pastor from a local taquería after a long hackathon session.

info.persona: Terrell Piperno blends relentless organization with a fiercely competitive edge, turning every codebase, model kit, and workout into a precision challenge, though they sometimes hoard unfinished projects and skip meals when deep in a sprint.
info.professional_persona: Terrell Piperno, a senior software engineer specializing in full‑stack development, cloud architecture, and data engineering, leverages their analytical mindset and disciplined organization to design scalable, secure systems with Python, Java, and Go while leading Agile teams through meticulous sprint planning and code reviews, reflecting a competitive drive to meet high performance standards.
info.cultural_background: Terrell comes from an Italian‑American family that settled in the Midwest before moving to Texas. His upbringing blended traditional Italian customs—home‑cooked meals, strong family ties, and seasonal celebrations—with the contemporary suburban culture of Keller, TX. He participates in local community events, attends the Catholic church on holidays, and enjoys both Italian cuisine and Texas barbecue. His cultural identity is rooted in a respect for hard work, self‑reliance, and community involvement, reflecting both his ethnic heritage and the Texan values of hospitality and competitiveness.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In his spare time, Terrell enjoys activities that blend structure with creative problem‑solving. He builds detailed model kits (airplanes, cars) and engages in woodworking projects that require precise measurement and planning. He is an avid chess player, regularly competing in local club tournaments, and follows the Dallas Cowboys and NFL closely. He maintains a disciplined fitness routine, focusing on weightlifting and functional training. He also likes cooking grilled meals for his family, experimenting with classic Italian recipes that reflect his heritage, and volunteering as a mentor for a regional STEM outreach program.
info.sports_persona: Terrell Piperno follows the Dallas Cowboys avidly each NFL season, supports the Texas Rangers during summer, trains at CrossFit Dallas three times a week, participates in local weightlifting meets, and hikes the Texas Hill Country with family on weekends, blending competitive spirit with a disciplined fitness routine.
info.arts_persona: Terrell Piperno channels creative problem‑solving into building detailed model kits of historic aircraft while appreciating the precision of Leonardo da Vinci’s sketches, listens to classic rock legends like Led Zeppelin and modern film composer Hans Zimmer, and attends annual art installations at the Dallas Museum of Art featuring contemporary artists such as Yayoi Kusama.
info.travel_persona: Terrell Piperno prefers meticulously planned road trips, having explored Austin, New Mexico’s Santa Fe, and Chicago using a custom spreadsheet itinerary, and dreams of visiting Kyoto’s temples, the Italian Amalfi Coast, and Reykjavik’s geothermal pools, balancing family obligations with a desire for immersive cultural experiences.
info.culinary_persona: Terrell Piperno enjoys grilling ribeye steaks seasoned with rosemary and garlic, perfecting classic Italian dishes like Spaghetti Carbonara and Margherita pizza on a home‑made stone oven, and experiments with fresh basil, sun‑dried tomatoes, and smoked mozzarella, showcasing a competent yet adventurous cooking style.

info.persona: Sunny Delapaz is a quietly driven art‑enthusiast who balances meticulous office management with spontaneous street photography, a habit of late‑night museum visits, and a tendency to over‑schedule community workshops despite a love for solitary garden walks.
info.professional_persona: Sunny Delapaz is a front‑desk specialist with a talent for juggling appointment schedules, data entry, and visitor relations, leveraging their curiosity for visual arts to design eye‑catching lobby displays while preparing to step into an office‑manager role within two years.
info.cultural_background: Sunny grew up in a middle‑class, suburban environment near Houston, raised by parents of Anglo‑American and Hispanic descent, which gave her a blended cultural perspective. Though she identifies as white, the Delapaz surname reflects a family heritage that celebrates both Southern hospitality and the vibrant multicultural tapestry of Fort Bend County. She was exposed to diverse traditions through community festivals, bilingual neighbors, and a local school curriculum that emphasized respect for varied cultural expressions. This upbringing fostered her appreciation for art, openness to unconventional ideas, and a strong sense of community responsibility.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In her free time, Sunny immerses herself in the visual arts scene, regularly visiting galleries and museums in Houston and Fort Bend County. She practices photography, focusing on candid street scenes and local architecture, and enjoys experimenting with cooking, often trying recipes inspired by the diverse cultures around her. Her curiosity drives her to attend craft workshops—such as pottery and watercolor painting—and to read a mix of contemporary fiction, non‑fiction on creativity, and art history. She also tends a modest garden, goes on nature walks, and volunteers occasionally at community art outreach programs, preferring small, intimate groups.
info.sports_persona: Sunny Delapaz enjoys Saturday morning jogs along Buffalo Bayou, follows the Houston Astros in baseball and the Houston Rockets in basketball, participates in a local community Pilates class, and cheers on the Houston Dynamo during the MLS season, balancing a laid‑back approach to exercise with occasional competitive spirit in weekend softball leagues.
info.arts_persona: Sunny Delapaz immerses themselves in the Houston art scene, curating personal photo series of street murals inspired by the bold colors of Frida Kahlo and the contemporary work of Kehinde Wiley, while listening to Leon Bridges and Lila Downs during studio sessions, and attending performances of the Houston Symphony and the plays of local playwrights such as Diana Kipnis.
info.travel_persona: Sunny Delapaz prefers thoughtfully planned weekend getaways that blend photography opportunities with cultural immersion, having explored the historic districts of San Antonio, the culinary streets of Oaxaca, and the avant‑garde art installations of Marfa, while dreaming of a month‑long study tour of European museums in Paris, Florence, and Barcelona.
info.culinary_persona: Sunny Delapaz enjoys experimenting in the kitchen, skillfully preparing dishes like chile‑relleno enchiladas with fresh cilantro, cumin, and poblano peppers, homemade shrimp tacos topped with mango salsa, and occasional forays into Japanese ramen using miso, kombu broth, and soft‑boiled eggs, while also tending a herb garden that supplies basil and thyme for weeknight meals.
